summary: Ready: 0 blockers and 0 warnings of 31 checks (develop @ a1b2c3d4, app, docker/systemd).

results.title: The repo has a .gitlab-ci.yml
results.why: Without a CI file GitLab builds no pipeline for the repo.
results.fix:
include:
  - project: northwind/deployment
    ref: main
    file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml

results.title: The CI file includes northwind/deployment (app or package template)
results.why: The shared engine supplies build, deploy, lock and verify; a repo outside it is not on the pipeline.
results.fix:
include:
  - project: northwind/deployment
    ref: main
    file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml    # a service
    # file: cicd/package.gitlab-ci.yml  # an npm library

results.title: The env branches exist (develop, pre-release, release; a package needs develop and release)
results.why: The workflow rules run only on these names; 'prerelease' or 'developer' never deploys.
results.fix:
git switch -c develop origin/<default> && git push origin develop
git switch -c pre-release origin/develop && git push origin pre-release
git switch -c release origin/pre-release && git push origin release

results.evidence: EXECUTOR resolves for every env branch.
results.title: EXECUTOR is set per environment (docker or systemd)
results.why: Without EXECUTOR no build/deploy job matches and the pipeline is empty.
results.fix:
EXECUTOR  scope develop  = docker
EXECUTOR  scope *        = systemd

results.title: TARGET_HOSTS names the right inventory group per environment
results.why: Without it the engine targets the group named after the branch; [release] is the stage hosts (PRD-1).
results.fix:
TARGET_HOSTS  scope pre-release = pre-<group>
TARGET_HOSTS  scope release     = main-<group>

results.evidence: DOTENV is a File variable for every env.
results.title: DOTENV is a File variable for every environment
results.why: prepare_systemd_inputs requires a readable File variable; Docker bakes it at build time.
results.fix:
DOTENV  type File  scope develop / pre-release / release (release: Protected)
# content: the keys of .env.sample, KEY=value per line

results.evidence: NODE_VERSION set for the systemd envs.
results.title: NODE_VERSION is a full x.y.z for systemd environments
results.why: deploy-systemd installs this version with nvm on air-gapped hosts; a missing value fails the deploy.
results.fix:
NODE_VERSION  scope pre-release = 20.19.0
NODE_VERSION  scope release     = 20.19.0

results.title: DOTENV of develop and pre-release names no production host
results.why: Stage must never reach production (guardrail 4).
results.fix: # point the listed keys at stage (192.168.73.x) or pre-release (10.21.63.x / 10.21.93.21) services

results.title: package.json parses and has name, version and scripts
results.why: The engine runs npm ci and npm run; both need a valid package.json.

results.title: package-lock.json is committed
results.why: Docker copies package-lock.json and runs npm ci; systemd runs npm ci. Without a lock the build fails or floats.
results.fix:
# under the target Node version:
npm install --package-lock-only
git add package-lock.json && git commit -m 'build: commit package-lock.json'

results.title: package-lock.json matches package.json
results.why: npm ci refuses a lock that is out of sync (EUSAGE) and the build fails before any code runs.
results.source: JOB-MODEL §1.2 (lockfile first); triage rule lock-out-of-sync; KB runtime/mongoose-duplicate-copy
results.fix:
# under the target Node version, for each listed package:
npm install <pkg>@<range> --package-lock-only
# never delete the lockfile to 'fix' it

results.evidence: No routing variable in the CI file.
results.title: Routing variables are not set in .gitlab-ci.yml
results.why: A value in the file applies to every branch: a production group in it sends develop to production (guardrail 4).
results.fix:
# remove these lines from .gitlab-ci.yml and set them in Settings -> CI/CD -> Variables, scoped per environment:
#   EXECUTOR@develop=docker, EXECUTOR@*=systemd, TARGET_HOSTS@pre-release=pre-<group>, TARGET_HOSTS@release=main-<group>

results.title: The CI file only includes the engine (no job or workflow overrides)
results.why: Overriding build/deploy/workflow breaks the lock, the two-move publish and the verify step.
results.fix: # keep the file to the include block; move custom jobs to a reviewed MR on northwind/deployment

results.title: pre-release and release are protected (Developers cannot push)
results.why: An unprotected release lets any Developer deploy to production and read protected variables.
results.fix: release, pre-release: Allowed to merge = Maintainers, Allowed to push = No one, force push off

results.title: An .env.sample lists the keys the service reads
results.why: Operators build DOTENV per environment from it; without it a missing key is found by a failed deploy.
results.fix:
PORT=3000
MONGO_URI=
REDIS_HOST=
# one KEY= per line, no values

results.evidence: No .env or key file in the repo root.
results.title: No .env, private key or npm token is committed
results.why: A committed secret is readable by every project member and every fork (guardrail 7). It does not stop the pipeline, so it is a warning here; 28 front-ends commit .env.local (estate sweep 2026-10-22).
results.fix:
.env
*.pem
# remove the file: git rm --cached .env && rotate every value it held

results.title: lockfileVersion matches the Node runtime
results.why: A v2/v3 lock on a Node 14 runtime pulls transitive deps that crash on old syntax (||=).
results.fix:
# regenerate with the runtime's npm: Node 14 -> lockfileVersion 1, Node >= 16 -> 2 or 3
npm install --package-lock-only

results.title: The lockfile resolves from the internal npm mirror
results.why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet and argus-01.dev does not resolve on production; npm 6 (lockfileVersion 1) fetches resolved URLs as written.
results.fix:
# rewrite only the host prefix of resolved URLs, e.g.
sed -i 's#https://registry.dev.northwind.example/repository/npm-group/#https://npm-mirror.prod.northwind.example/#' package-lock.json

results.title: The Node version is declared (engines.node or .nvmrc)
results.why: systemd installs NODE_VERSION and Docker picks a base image; a repo that does not say which Node it needs gets mismatches.
results.fix:
"engines": { "node": ">=20 <21" }
# and/or .nvmrc: 20.19.0

results.title: engines, .nvmrc and the Dockerfile agree on the Node major
results.why: Different majors mean the build and the runtime use different Node versions.
results.fix: # align all of them on one major, e.g. 20

results.title: The start script the runtime calls exists
results.why: The images run npm run $RUN_SCRIPT (start, start:prod for nestjs); a missing script fails with 'Missing script: start'.

results.title: TypeScript and NestJS repos have a build script
results.why: detect_project_type defaults BUILD_SCRIPTS to build for ts/nestjs and the image runs npm run build.
results.fix: "scripts": { "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json" }

results.title: The TypeScript build writes to dist/
results.why: The runtime image copies only dist, node_modules and package.json.
results.fix:
"compilerOptions": { "outDir": "dist" }
# non-TS assets (*.graphql): nest-cli.json "assets" or a postbuild copy

results.title: Native modules are known (air-gapped hosts)
results.why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet: node-gyp cannot download headers.
results.fix: NPM_CI_FLAGS  scope pre-release/release = --nodedir=/root/.nvm/versions/node/v<NODE_VERSION>

results.title: The include ref is main
results.why: Every consumer uses ref main; another ref freezes the repo on an old engine.
results.fix: ref: main

results.title: The head commit does not carry [skip ci]
results.why: A [skip ci] head builds no pipeline, so the env shows nothing to deploy.
results.fix: git commit --allow-empty -m 'chore: trigger pipeline' && git push

results.title: A committed .npmrc carries no token
results.why: handle_npmrc writes the registry; a committed token leaks and overrides the engine's.
results.fix: # delete .npmrc or keep only non-secret lines; the engine writes the @northwind registry and token itself

results.title: Docker build has a Dockerfile or a template
results.why: A repo Dockerfile always wins; without one the nodejs-js template is used, which is wrong for nestjs/nextjs.
results.fix: DOCKERFILE_NAME  scope develop = nestjs   # one of: nodejs-js, nodejs-ts, nestjs, nextjs, nextjs-standalone, vite-spa, golang, python, nginx …

results.title: systemd unit and directory follow northwind-<slug>
results.why: Overrides break verify, inventory and unitinfo globs; the operator's rule is CI slug naming.
results.fix: # remove SYSTEMD_SERVICE / SYSTEMD_APP_DIR; the engine uses northwind-<group>-<repo>.service in /data/services/northwind-<group>-<repo>

results.evidence: develop success, pre-release success, release manual
results.title: The newest pipeline on each env branch passed
results.why: A repo that meets the requirements can still be red for code reasons; shown for context.
results.fix: # open the failing pipeline in Argus CI/CD -> Failures for the class and the fix

results.title: Service-info.md describes the service
results.why: Argus and Outline docs read it; convention, not required by the engine.
results.fix: # Service-info.md: purpose, ports, dependencies, env keys, owners

results.title: An npm package is named @northwind/*
results.why: The package template publishes to the @northwind registry (project 213).
results.fix: "name": "@northwind/<name>"

results.title: Package version follows the branch rule
results.why: npm_publish refuses any other format, and never republishes an existing version.
results.fix:
"version": "1.4.0-alpha.0"   # develop / pre-release
"version": "1.4.0"           # release

results.title: A package that needs a build declares it
results.why: The package template builds only when BUILD_NEEDED=true and publishes dist/ or build/.
results.fix:
"scripts": { "build": "tsc" }
BUILD_NEEDED = true   # CI variable; artifacts are dist/ and build/ only

handoff.prompt:
# Make northwind/legacy/legacy-web ready for the shared CI/CD pipeline

Goal: the repository northwind/legacy/legacy-web (GitLab project 502, https://glab.northwind.example/northwind/legacy/legacy-web) must meet the requirements of the shared
pipeline (northwind/deployment). Argus's readiness check of `develop` @ `cccccccccc` found the file
problems below. Fix only these, in the repository, on a new branch.

## Guardrails
- Work on a new branch `fix/ci-readiness` from `develop`; open a merge request into `develop`.
- Never push to develop, pre-release, release, main or master; never force-push; never merge the MR yourself.
- Never change CI/CD variables, branch protection or project settings; never run, retry or play a pipeline.
- Never commit a secret (.env with values, tokens, keys). `.env.sample` has keys only, no values.
- Regenerate `package-lock.json` only with the Node version the service runs on, and only with
  `npm install --package-lock-only` (never delete the lockfile).

## Steps
1. **The repo has a .gitlab-ci.yml** — `.gitlab-ci.yml` — evidence: No .gitlab-ci.yml on develop (.gitlab-ci.yml)
   Why: Without a CI file GitLab builds no pipeline for the repo.
   Change:
   ```
   include:
     - project: northwind/deployment
       ref: main
       file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml
   ```
2. **The CI file includes northwind/deployment (app or package template)** — `.gitlab-ci.yml` — evidence: No CI file, so no include. (.gitlab-ci.yml)
   Why: The shared engine supplies build, deploy, lock and verify; a repo outside it is not on the pipeline.
   Change:
   ```
   include:
     - project: northwind/deployment
       ref: main
       file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml    # a service
       # file: cicd/package.gitlab-ci.yml  # an npm library
   ```
3. **package-lock.json is committed** — `package-lock.json` — evidence: No package-lock.json (yarn.lock found: the engine runs npm ci). (package-lock.json)
   Why: Docker copies package-lock.json and runs npm ci; systemd runs npm ci. Without a lock the build fails or floats.
   Change:
   ```
   # under the target Node version:
   npm install --package-lock-only
   git add package-lock.json && git commit -m 'build: commit package-lock.json'
   ```
4. **An .env.sample lists the keys the service reads** — `.env.sample` — evidence: No .env.sample / .env.example in the repo root. (repo root)
   Why: Operators build DOTENV per environment from it; without it a missing key is found by a failed deploy.
   Change:
   ```
   PORT=3000
   MONGO_URI=
   REDIS_HOST=
   # one KEY= per line, no values
   ```
5. **No .env, private key or npm token is committed** — `.gitignore` — evidence: Committed: .env (.env)
   Why: A committed secret is readable by every project member and every fork (guardrail 7). It does not stop the pipeline, so it is a warning here; 28 front-ends commit .env.local (estate sweep 2026-10-22).
   Change:
   ```
   .env
   *.pem
   # remove the file: git rm --cached .env && rotate every value it held
   ```
6. **The Node version is declared (engines.node or .nvmrc)** — `package.json` — evidence: No engines.node, .nvmrc or node image in a Dockerfile. (package.json)
   Why: systemd installs NODE_VERSION and Docker picks a base image; a repo that does not say which Node it needs gets mismatches.
   Change:
   ```
   "engines": { "node": ">=20 <21" }
   # and/or .nvmrc: 20.19.0
   ```
7. **The start script the runtime calls exists** — `package.json` — evidence: No "start" script: the image runs npm run start. (package.json)
   Why: The images run npm run $RUN_SCRIPT (start, start:prod for nestjs); a missing script fails with 'Missing script: start'.
   Change:
   ```
   "scripts": {
     "start": "node dist/main.js",
     "start:prod": "node dist/main.js"
   }
   ```
8. **Native modules are known (air-gapped hosts)** — `package.json / NPM_CI_FLAGS` — evidence: Native modules: bcrypt (package.json)
   Why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet: node-gyp cannot download headers.
   Change:
   ```
   NPM_CI_FLAGS  scope pre-release/release = --nodedir=/root/.nvm/versions/node/v<NODE_VERSION>
   ```

## Not yours (the operator does these in GitLab settings)
- The env branches exist (develop, pre-release, release; a package needs develop and release): Missing: pre-release, release (found master)

## Verify
- `npm ci` succeeds locally under the target Node version (when package.json changed).
- The MR pipeline (if any) is green; describe each change in the MR description with the check id.

## Report back
The MR link, the list of check ids you fixed, and anything you could not fix with the reason.

results.why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet and argus-01.dev does not resolve on production; npm 6 (lockfileVersion 1) fetches resolved URLs as written.
results.fix:
# rewrite only the host prefix of resolved URLs, e.g.
sed -i 's#https://registry.dev.northwind.example/repository/npm-group/#https://npm-mirror.prod.northwind.example/#' package-lock.json

results.evidence: develop failed, pre-release none, release success
results.title: The newest pipeline on each env branch passed
results.why: A repo that meets the requirements can still be red for code reasons; shown for context.
results.fix: # open the failing pipeline in Argus CI/CD -> Failures for the class and the fix

results.title: The repo has a .gitlab-ci.yml
results.why: Without a CI file GitLab builds no pipeline for the repo.
results.fix:
include:
  - project: northwind/deployment
    ref: main
    file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml

results.title: The CI file includes northwind/deployment (app or package template)
results.why: The shared engine supplies build, deploy, lock and verify; a repo outside it is not on the pipeline.
results.fix:
include:
  - project: northwind/deployment
    ref: main
    file: cicd/app.gitlab-ci.yml    # a service
    # file: cicd/package.gitlab-ci.yml  # an npm library

results.title: The env branches exist (develop, pre-release, release; a package needs develop and release)
results.why: The workflow rules run only on these names; 'prerelease' or 'developer' never deploys.
results.fix:
git switch -c develop origin/<default> && git push origin develop
git switch -c pre-release origin/develop && git push origin pre-release
git switch -c release origin/pre-release && git push origin release

results.title: package.json parses and has name, version and scripts
results.why: The engine runs npm ci and npm run; both need a valid package.json.

results.title: package-lock.json is committed
results.why: Docker copies package-lock.json and runs npm ci; systemd runs npm ci. Without a lock the build fails or floats.
results.fix:
# under the target Node version:
npm install --package-lock-only
git add package-lock.json && git commit -m 'build: commit package-lock.json'

results.title: package-lock.json matches package.json
results.why: npm ci refuses a lock that is out of sync (EUSAGE) and the build fails before any code runs.
results.source: JOB-MODEL §1.2 (lockfile first); triage rule lock-out-of-sync; KB runtime/mongoose-duplicate-copy
results.fix:
# under the target Node version, for each listed package:
npm install <pkg>@<range> --package-lock-only
# never delete the lockfile to 'fix' it

results.title: An npm package is named @northwind/*
results.why: The package template publishes to the @northwind registry (project 213).
results.fix: "name": "@northwind/<name>"

results.title: Package version follows the branch rule
results.why: npm_publish refuses any other format, and never republishes an existing version.
results.fix:
"version": "1.4.0-alpha.0"   # develop / pre-release
"version": "1.4.0"           # release

results.title: pre-release and release are protected (Developers cannot push)
results.why: An unprotected release lets any Developer deploy to production and read protected variables.
results.fix: release, pre-release: Allowed to merge = Maintainers, Allowed to push = No one, force push off

results.evidence: No .env or key file in the repo root.
results.title: No .env, private key or npm token is committed
results.why: A committed secret is readable by every project member and every fork (guardrail 7). It does not stop the pipeline, so it is a warning here; 28 front-ends commit .env.local (estate sweep 2026-10-22).
results.fix:
.env
*.pem
# remove the file: git rm --cached .env && rotate every value it held

results.title: TypeScript and NestJS repos have a build script
results.why: detect_project_type defaults BUILD_SCRIPTS to build for ts/nestjs and the image runs npm run build.
results.fix: "scripts": { "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json" }

results.title: A package that needs a build declares it
results.why: The package template builds only when BUILD_NEEDED=true and publishes dist/ or build/.
results.fix:
"scripts": { "build": "tsc" }
BUILD_NEEDED = true   # CI variable; artifacts are dist/ and build/ only

results.title: The include ref is main
results.why: Every consumer uses ref main; another ref freezes the repo on an old engine.
results.fix: ref: main

results.title: The head commit does not carry [skip ci]
results.why: A [skip ci] head builds no pipeline, so the env shows nothing to deploy.
results.fix: git commit --allow-empty -m 'chore: trigger pipeline' && git push

results.title: A committed .npmrc carries no token
results.why: handle_npmrc writes the registry; a committed token leaks and overrides the engine's.
results.fix: # delete .npmrc or keep only non-secret lines; the engine writes the @northwind registry and token itself

results.title: EXECUTOR is set per environment (docker or systemd)
results.why: Without EXECUTOR no build/deploy job matches and the pipeline is empty.
results.fix:
EXECUTOR  scope develop  = docker
EXECUTOR  scope *        = systemd

results.title: TARGET_HOSTS names the right inventory group per environment
results.why: Without it the engine targets the group named after the branch; [release] is the stage hosts (PRD-1).
results.fix:
TARGET_HOSTS  scope pre-release = pre-<group>
TARGET_HOSTS  scope release     = main-<group>

results.title: DOTENV is a File variable for every environment
results.why: prepare_systemd_inputs requires a readable File variable; Docker bakes it at build time.
results.fix:
DOTENV  type File  scope develop / pre-release / release (release: Protected)
# content: the keys of .env.sample, KEY=value per line

results.title: NODE_VERSION is a full x.y.z for systemd environments
results.why: deploy-systemd installs this version with nvm on air-gapped hosts; a missing value fails the deploy.
results.fix:
NODE_VERSION  scope pre-release = 20.19.0
NODE_VERSION  scope release     = 20.19.0

results.title: DOTENV of develop and pre-release names no production host
results.why: Stage must never reach production (guardrail 4).
results.fix: # point the listed keys at stage (192.168.73.x) or pre-release (10.21.63.x / 10.21.93.21) services

results.title: Routing variables are not set in .gitlab-ci.yml
results.why: A value in the file applies to every branch: a production group in it sends develop to production (guardrail 4).
results.fix:
# remove these lines from .gitlab-ci.yml and set them in Settings -> CI/CD -> Variables, scoped per environment:
#   EXECUTOR@develop=docker, EXECUTOR@*=systemd, TARGET_HOSTS@pre-release=pre-<group>, TARGET_HOSTS@release=main-<group>

results.title: The CI file only includes the engine (no job or workflow overrides)
results.why: Overriding build/deploy/workflow breaks the lock, the two-move publish and the verify step.
results.fix: # keep the file to the include block; move custom jobs to a reviewed MR on northwind/deployment

results.title: An .env.sample lists the keys the service reads
results.why: Operators build DOTENV per environment from it; without it a missing key is found by a failed deploy.
results.fix:
PORT=3000
MONGO_URI=
REDIS_HOST=
# one KEY= per line, no values

results.title: lockfileVersion matches the Node runtime
results.why: A v2/v3 lock on a Node 14 runtime pulls transitive deps that crash on old syntax (||=).
results.fix:
# regenerate with the runtime's npm: Node 14 -> lockfileVersion 1, Node >= 16 -> 2 or 3
npm install --package-lock-only

results.title: The Node version is declared (engines.node or .nvmrc)
results.why: systemd installs NODE_VERSION and Docker picks a base image; a repo that does not say which Node it needs gets mismatches.
results.fix:
"engines": { "node": ">=20 <21" }
# and/or .nvmrc: 20.19.0

results.title: engines, .nvmrc and the Dockerfile agree on the Node major
results.why: Different majors mean the build and the runtime use different Node versions.
results.fix: # align all of them on one major, e.g. 20

results.title: The start script the runtime calls exists
results.why: The images run npm run $RUN_SCRIPT (start, start:prod for nestjs); a missing script fails with 'Missing script: start'.

results.title: The TypeScript build writes to dist/
results.why: The runtime image copies only dist, node_modules and package.json.
results.fix:
"compilerOptions": { "outDir": "dist" }
# non-TS assets (*.graphql): nest-cli.json "assets" or a postbuild copy

results.title: Native modules are known (air-gapped hosts)
results.why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet: node-gyp cannot download headers.
results.fix: NPM_CI_FLAGS  scope pre-release/release = --nodedir=/root/.nvm/versions/node/v<NODE_VERSION>

results.title: Docker build has a Dockerfile or a template
results.why: A repo Dockerfile always wins; without one the nodejs-js template is used, which is wrong for nestjs/nextjs.
results.fix: DOCKERFILE_NAME  scope develop = nestjs   # one of: nodejs-js, nodejs-ts, nestjs, nextjs, nextjs-standalone, vite-spa, golang, python, nginx …

results.title: systemd unit and directory follow northwind-<slug>
results.why: Overrides break verify, inventory and unitinfo globs; the operator's rule is CI slug naming.
results.fix: # remove SYSTEMD_SERVICE / SYSTEMD_APP_DIR; the engine uses northwind-<group>-<repo>.service in /data/services/northwind-<group>-<repo>

results.title: Service-info.md describes the service
results.why: Argus and Outline docs read it; convention, not required by the engine.
results.fix: # Service-info.md: purpose, ports, dependencies, env keys, owners

options.title: Fix the repo files on a branch fix/ci-readiness and open an MR
options.what: The lockfile resolves from the internal npm mirror (package-lock.json)
options.why: These are file changes the pipeline needs before the first build can pass.

options.approval: a maintainer reviews and merges the MR

handoff.prompt:
# Make northwind/packages/techno_models_ts ready for the shared CI/CD pipeline

Goal: the repository northwind/packages/techno_models_ts (GitLab project 503, https://glab.northwind.example/northwind/packages/techno_models_ts) must meet the requirements of the shared
pipeline (northwind/deployment). Argus's readiness check of `develop` @ `dddddddddd` found the file
problems below. Fix only these, in the repository, on a new branch.

## Guardrails
- Work on a new branch `fix/ci-readiness` from `develop`; open a merge request into `develop`.
- Never push to develop, pre-release, release, main or master; never force-push; never merge the MR yourself.
- Never change CI/CD variables, branch protection or project settings; never run, retry or play a pipeline.
- Never commit a secret (.env with values, tokens, keys). `.env.sample` has keys only, no values.
- Regenerate `package-lock.json` only with the Node version the service runs on, and only with
  `npm install --package-lock-only` (never delete the lockfile).

## Steps
1. **The lockfile resolves from the internal npm mirror** — `package-lock.json` — evidence: resolved from registry.dev.northwind.example (1, dev-only mirror, does not resolve on production) (first 96 KB) (package-lock.json)
   Why: pre-release and release hosts have no internet and argus-01.dev does not resolve on production; npm 6 (lockfileVersion 1) fetches resolved URLs as written.
   Change:
   ```
   # rewrite only the host prefix of resolved URLs, e.g.
   sed -i 's#https://registry.dev.northwind.example/repository/npm-group/#https://npm-mirror.prod.northwind.example/#' package-lock.json
   ```

## Not yours (the operator does these in GitLab settings)
- none

## Verify
- `npm ci` succeeds locally under the target Node version (when package.json changed).
- The MR pipeline (if any) is green; describe each change in the MR description with the check id.

## Report back
The MR link, the list of check ids you fixed, and anything you could not fix with the reason.
